author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: valid and payload cross rst_a_n to rst_b_n through separate per-bit synchronisers. A source-only reset during a transfer can let the active consumer see the old valid with a partly cleared payload and commit a word that was never sent.

author_reading.rationale: The valid and payload registers share one asynchronous source reset, so a source reset cannot leave a valid without its cleared payload.

labels.rationale: vld_a_q is reset, unlike c02, so the valid cannot carry a stale 1 out of reset. The independent resets remain a protocol matter, not a reset-structure defect.

While the consumer remains active, producer reset clears payload and valid through independent paths. Those paths can present the reset payload with the old valid, committing a word that the producer did not send.
labels.suspected_flaw: Independent payload-bit synchronisers also permit incoherent ordinary transfers, and there is no reciprocal acknowledgement.

settlement.rationale: B is right: the shared source reset does not make the consumer tolerant. The reset clears valid and payload through independent synchroniser paths, so the consumer can commit a mixed word. A (and the author) treat a reset valid as sufficient. This is RDC-005's unproved destination tolerance. The parallel payload synchroniser is also a CDC defect outside the RDC deck.
